## Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(rsample)
library(dplyr)
library(janitor)
library(tidymodels)
library(baguette)
library(rpart.plot)


# Read from URL
bike_url <- "https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/datasets/SeoulBikeData.csv"
raw_data <- read_csv(bike_url, locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"))
```

```{r}

    temp = temperature_c,

    visibility = visibility_10m,
    dew_point_temp = dew_point_temperature_c,
    solar_radiation = solar_radiation_mj_m2,
    rainfall = rainfall_mm,
    snowfall = snowfall_cm,

```

After aggregating the data, I recreated summary statistics for the numeric variables and examined bike rentals across seasons and holidays. Also created visualizations to explore the relationships between daily bike rentals and weather conditions, including temperature, humidity, and rainfall.

Calculated a correlation matrix to examine the relationships between the numeric variables. The results help identify which weather conditions have the strongest positive or negative linear relationships with daily bike rentals. And it seems temperature and dew point have the strongest correlation

## Split the Data

```{r split-data}
set.seed(558)
bike_split <- initial_split(daily_data, prop = 0.75, strata = seasons)
bike_train <- training(bike_split)
bike_test  <- testing(bike_split)

bike_cv_folds <- vfold_cv(bike_train, v = 10)
```

## Fitting MLR Models

### Recipes

```{r recipes}
rec1 <- recipe(bike_count ~ ., data = bike_train) |>
  update_role(date, new_role = "ID") |>
  step_date(date, features = "dow") |>
  step_mutate(day_type = factor(if_else(date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
                                        "Weekend", "Weekday"))) |>
  step_rm(date_dow) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(seasons, holiday, day_type)

rec2 <- rec1 |>
  step_interact(terms = ~ starts_with("seasons"):starts_with("holiday") +
                  starts_with("seasons"):temp) |>
  step_interact(terms = ~ temp:rainfall)

rec3 <- rec2 |>
  step_mutate(temp_sq = temp^2, humidity_sq = humidity^2)
```

### Fit with 10-fold CV

```{r mlr-cv}
lm_spec <- linear_reg() |>
  set_engine("lm")

wf1 <- workflow() |> add_recipe(rec1) |> add_model(lm_spec)
wf2 <- workflow() |> add_recipe(rec2) |> add_model(lm_spec)
wf3 <- workflow() |> add_recipe(rec3) |> add_model(lm_spec)

cv_fit1 <- wf1 |> fit_resamples(bike_cv_folds)
cv_fit2 <- wf2 |> fit_resamples(bike_cv_folds)
cv_fit3 <- wf3 |> fit_resamples(bike_cv_folds)

bind_rows(
  collect_metrics(cv_fit1) |> mutate(model = "Recipe 1: main effects"),
  collect_metrics(cv_fit2) |> mutate(model = "Recipe 2: + interactions"),
  collect_metrics(cv_fit3) |> mutate(model = "Recipe 3: + squared temp & humidity")
) |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)
```

Recipe 3 has the lowest CV RMSE mean at 3038.551

### Best MLR model on the full training set

```{r mlr-final}
# Replace wf3 with the workflow that had the lowest CV RMSE
mlr_final <- last_fit(wf3, split = bike_split,
                      metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))
```

## Fitting Other Models

All three models use the first recipe and are tuned with the same 10 CV folds.

### Regression Tree

```{r tree}
tree_spec <- decision_tree(cost_complexity = tune(),
                           tree_depth = tune()) |>
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")

tree_wf <- workflow() |> add_recipe(rec1) |> add_model(tree_spec)

tree_grid <- grid_regular(cost_complexity(), tree_depth(),
                          levels = c(10, 5))

set.seed(558)
tree_tuned <- tune_grid(tree_wf, resamples = bike_cv_folds,
                        grid = tree_grid,
                        metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))

tree_best <- select_best(tree_tuned, metric = "rmse")
tree_best

tree_final_wf <- finalize_workflow(tree_wf, tree_best)
tree_final <- last_fit(tree_final_wf, split = bike_split,
                       metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))
```

### Bagged Tree

```{r bag}
bag_spec <- bag_tree(cost_complexity = tune(),
                     tree_depth = tune(),
                     min_n = tune()) |>
  set_engine("rpart", times = 25) |>
  set_mode("regression")

bag_wf <- workflow() |> add_recipe(rec1) |> add_model(bag_spec)

bag_grid <- grid_regular(cost_complexity(), tree_depth(), min_n(),
                         levels = 3)

set.seed(558)
bag_tuned <- tune_grid(bag_wf, resamples = bike_cv_folds,
                       grid = bag_grid,
                       metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))

bag_best <- select_best(bag_tuned, metric = "rmse")
bag_best

bag_final_wf <- finalize_workflow(bag_wf, bag_best)
bag_final <- last_fit(bag_final_wf, split = bike_split,
                      metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))
```

### Random Forest

```{r rf}
# importance must be requested in the engine so we can plot it later
rf_spec <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 500) |>
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "permutation") |>
  set_mode("regression")

rf_wf <- workflow() |> add_recipe(rec1) |> add_model(rf_spec)

# rec1 produces 13 predictors, so mtry can range from 1 to 13
rf_params <- extract_parameter_set_dials(rf_wf) |>
  update(mtry = mtry(c(1, 13)))

rf_grid <- grid_regular(rf_params, levels = c(mtry = 5, min_n = 4))

set.seed(558)
rf_tuned <- tune_grid(rf_wf, resamples = bike_cv_folds,
                      grid = rf_grid,
                      metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))

rf_best <- select_best(rf_tuned, metric = "rmse")
rf_best

rf_final_wf <- finalize_workflow(rf_wf, rf_best)
rf_final <- last_fit(rf_final_wf, split = bike_split,
                     metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))
```

## Compare on the Test Set

```{r compare}
bind_rows(
  collect_metrics(mlr_final)  |> mutate(model = "MLR"),
  collect_metrics(tree_final) |> mutate(model = "Regression tree"),
  collect_metrics(bag_final)  |> mutate(model = "Bagged tree"),
  collect_metrics(rf_final)   |> mutate(model = "Random forest")
) |>
  select(model, .metric, .estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = .metric, values_from = .estimate) |>
  arrange(rmse)
```

RF performed best on both metrics on the test set with an RMSE of \~2,332 and MAE of \~1,863 rentals per day. Both tree ensembles clearly beat the MLR model (RMSE \~3,059, MAE \~2,132), while the single regression tree performed worst (RMSE \~3,491, MAE \~2,496). RF chosen as overall best model and fit to the entire data set since it had the lowest error on both RMSE and MAE.

## Conclusion

The random forest was the best model on the test set (RMSE about 2,332, MAE about 1,863 rentals per day), clearly beating the bagged tree, MLR and single regression tree, so it's refit it on all 353 days. The tuned model used all 13 predictors at each split (mtry = 13) with a small node size, and it explains about 92% of the variance in daily rentals (OOB R² ≈ 0.92).
